html:
Merv was an oasis city in the Murghab delta of Turkmenistan, a major city of Central Asia from about the 6th century BCE until the 13th century CE. Its ruins cover a huge area near the modern town of Mary.

It was a province of the Persian Empire, then a Greek, Parthian and Sasanian city on the Silk Road. The Arab conquerors made it a base, and the revolt that brought the Abbasids to power began here in 747. Under the Seljuks it was a capital and, by some estimates, one of the largest cities in the world, with great libraries.

The Mongol sack of 1221 destroyed it. A smaller city was rebuilt beside the old one, but it never recovered. Its walls and the tomb of Sultan Sanjar are a World Heritage Site.
